name: Cao lau
summary: Cao lầu is Hoi An’s own noodle bowl: thick rice noodles barely wet with pork broth, under char siu, crisp ram, and Trà Quế herbs. Toss it while it is hot; it is not a soup you drink.
origin: Hoi An. People here call it bánh. The heritage centre describes thick noodles from local Xuyệt rice, soaked with wood-ash water from tràm on Cù Lao Chàm, milled with water from the Bá Lễ well, then steamed and cut. The bowl comes with a little pork broth, char siu, crispy ram, and Trà Quế herbs. It looks related to mì Quảng. It is a different dish.
howToEat: Toss it while it is hot. The broth wets the noodles.
Eat it at lunch. A cold takeaway misses the bowl.
where: The old town. The food hall inside Chợ Hội An, and the night market on Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng.
seoDescription: What cao lau is and why you should eat it in Hoi An.
